key_insight: DeepQuest turns knowledge gaps in Alzheimer's research into testable hypotheses, pairing automated experiments with separate audits of reliability and scientific contribution.
engineering_relevance: Research-agent pipelines can prioritize meaningful discovery by combining literature traceability, data-feasibility checks, hypothesis ranking, and evidence auditing.
method: Extract unresolved questions from domain reviews and formulate traceable hypotheses.
Screen data feasibility and prioritize hypotheses using groupwise Elo ranking.
Run iterative experiments and audit reliability separately from contribution against two frozen literature corpora.
evidence_signal: On OASIS-3, DeepQuest produced 42 feasible hypotheses, achieved a 95.24% audit-assessed scientific finding rate, and beat the strongest baselines in 14 of 15 reviewer–dimension comparisons; key associations were supported in ADNI and AIBL.
watch_item: Audit-assessed discovery depends on reviewer judgments and literature coverage; cohort associations alone do not establish causality or clinical utility.
paper_title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
